intervals.label: prototype detector (natural Ge crystals) at LNGS
intervals.note: Start: the installation month; data taking followed it. End: July 1999, as stated. 'About 15 month' of data taking.
intervals.quote: The HDMS prototype was installed at LNGS in March 1998 and successfully took data over a period of about 15 month, until July 1999

intervals.label: inner crystal replaced by enriched 73Ge; final setup installed
intervals.note: Bounds: the end of the prototype run (July 1999) and the installation of the final setup (August 2000: 'The final setup of the HDMS was installed at the LNGS in August 2000', arXiv:hep-ph/0206151, Sec. 2.2).
intervals.quote: the inner crystal of the detector has been replaced with a HPGe crystal of enriched 73 Ge

intervals.label: final setup (enriched 73Ge inner crystal) taking data
intervals.note: Start: August 2000 as stated. End: bounded by the last report read, a May 2006 conference paper that says the setup 'operates the first enriched 73Ge detector worldwide' (Physica Scripta T127, 2006); no source read gives a shutdown date.
intervals.quote: The final setup started data taking in Gran Sasso in August 2000.

intervals.label: completed (no shutdown date published)
intervals.note: Year of the last source read that reports HDMS operating (a conference paper of May 2006). No source read states when, or whether formally, HDMS stopped; the year is a bound on the latest evidence, not a published end date.
intervals.quote: The HDMS (Heidelberg Dark Matter Search) setup at LNGS, operates the first enriched {sup 73}Ge detector worldwide

threshold.quote: the energy threshold of 5 keV has been obtained for this measurement

summary.plain: HDMS, the Heidelberg Dark Matter Search, was a germanium experiment under the Gran Sasso mountain in Italy. A small germanium crystal sat inside a larger one that vetoed stray radiation, so it could look for dark matter particles recoiling off germanium nuclei. It reported limits on how strongly such particles can interact.
summary.technical: Two concentric HPGe detectors in one cryostat: a small p-type inner crystal (202 g in the prototype; later replaced by a crystal of enriched 73Ge, which adds spin-dependent sensitivity) is the WIMP target; a 2.1 kg well-type outer crystal is the anticoincidence shield. Prototype at LNGS March 1998 to July 1999 (natural Ge; 9.9 kg d, 2 keV threshold); final setup from August 2000 (5 keV threshold; 26.74 kg d in 2002; 85.48 kg d in a spin-dependent WIMP-neutron analysis cited in 2006).

technology.quote: Two concentric Ge crystals are housed by one cryostat system, the outer detector acting as an effective shield against multiple scattered photons for the inner crystal, which is the actual dark matter target.
technology.value: Two concentric high-purity germanium ionization detectors in one cryostat: inner target crystal inside a well-type outer anticoincidence crystal
